candidates.name: Texas Eastern Line 31 Expansion Project (Line 31 Loop and Line 14-P Lateral)
candidates.monitor_reason: no data center tie: about 19 km (11.8 mi), under the 25 km floor, and no validated ref ties the project or the Traceview plant to a data center
candidates.researcher_notes: This is a real Texas Eastern project with no row of its own. It is not an existing row under another name. The Federal Register scoping notice from March 2026 and a Gas Compression Magazine article from February 2026 describe a 10.2 mile 36-inch loop and a 1.6 mile 16-inch lateral to Entergy Mississippi's planned Traceview Advanced Power Station in Madison County, with 125,000 Dth/d of added capacity. The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects table for August 2026 (sheet Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, row 72) lists it as Applied, FERC docket CP26-75, cost $131 million, in service September 2028. Neither source names a data center customer. Press coverage links Entergy Mississippi to an Amazon Web Services campus in Madison County, but nothing found ties that load to Traceview or to this pipeline, so DataCenter stays blank. Revisit if the FERC filing or Entergy names a data center. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 3 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no.

candidates.name: Tiger Pipeline Richland Parish Lateral (Entergy Louisiana, Meta Hyperion supply)
candidates.researcher_notes: Energy Transfer and Entergy Louisiana signed a 20-year firm transport deal in November 2025. A 12-mile lateral off the Tiger Pipeline, up to 1 billion cubic feet per day, serves new Entergy gas plants and Meta's data center in Richland Parish. Trade press (Pipeline and Gas Journal, November 2025) names the lateral and the Meta data center. The Energy Information Administration August 2026 pipeline projects table (sheet Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, Excel row 123, listed as Tiger Pipeline Expansion Project) gives 12 miles, 1,000 million cubic feet per day, proposed, in service 2028, intrastate, and ties it to Entergy Louisiana's data center power plant. The Entergy press release was read and also describes the agreement. This is not P5849 (the operating 2011 Tiger expansion) and not P0265 (the main line). It is new pipe, so it is its own row. Start location was not stated by a source, so it is left blank. Delhi comes from the trade press as the delivery point. Capacity is 1,000 million cubic feet per day as the maximum; the firm contract is 250,000 MMBtu per day. Diameter, owner entity and cost were not found. The company holding the pipe is probably a Tiger Pipeline subsidiary of Energy Transfer, but no source names it, so Owner is left blank for the ownership team. A 13.24 mile figure from a FERC filing seen by one search was not verified and no FERC filing was found; EIA lists it as intrastate. Route not researched. Tier high: two independent sources agree on length and capacity. DataCenter is yes because trade press and EIA both name the Meta/Entergy data center supply. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 9 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no; tier high -> medium (9 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s); high needs at least one surviving ref).
